tasks.short: Explain how to use and care for the rented equipment, demonstrate it, look up instructions, give the customer a sheet and answer questions during the rental.

steps.what: Clerk explains to customers how to operate and care for the merchandise safely
Clerk demonstrates the equipment at the counter
Clerk looks up instructions for less familiar items in the manual binder
Clerk gives the customer the instruction sheet: copied by hand today; after the change printed only for customers without e-mail or who ask for paper
Clerk answers customers' phone questions about use during the rental

tasks.design: Each item's page in the rental system ({OTHER}) links to its manual, a one-page quick-start and safety notes, so the clerk finds them at once. The rental confirmation sends the customer the quick-start link, which answers some calls; explaining and demonstrating stay at the counter, and no chatbot answers customers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Instructions were in binders and copied by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Rental systems keep a page per item with availability and history.
tasks.still_hard: Quick-starts must be written for each item; safety advice must come from a person.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a customer has never used a floor sander and showing them twice.

reach.learn: Whether quick-start links cut misuse damage.

evidence.claim: A rental tool tracks availability and rental history per item with barcode check-in.
Shopping chatbots must tell customers they are AI; this design uses none.

assumptions: Boundary: from handing over the item to questions during the rental; repairs are outside.
Input contract: manuals and quick-starts loaded per item by the branch manager; fallback is the binder.

Explaining and demonstrating keep their full time. s3 keeps 40 because the manual is one click away but the clerk still reads it. s4 keeps 20 for printed sheets. s5 keeps 70 because the quick-start answers only simple calls.
Customer time is outside the clerk's savings.
unknowns: Number of items without a quick-start.
research_questions: Do quick-start links reduce use questions by phone?

incremental.description: Clerk reports items missing a quick-start.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the shop rents mostly familiar items, so few lookups and few calls change (13.2); high: many less familiar items with quick-starts (19.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Greet the customer, ask about the job, check what is available and discuss type, quality and quantity.

steps.what: Clerk greets customers at the counter
Clerk asks about the customer's job to find the right equipment
Clerk scans each returned item back in so the counter screen is current
Clerk checks availability: in the back and on the paper planning board today, on the counter screen after the change
Clerk discusses the type, quality and quantity of merchandise sought for rental

tasks.design: The counter screen of the rental system ({OTHER}) shows availability per item and date, including items out on rent and due back, instead of a walk to the back and a paper board. Greeting and advising the customer stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Availability lived on a planning board and in the clerk's head.
tasks.enabler_now: Rental systems track availability per item with barcode check-in and check-out.
tasks.still_hard: Availability is only right if every return is scanned.
tasks.human_edge: Talking a customer out of the wrong machine for their job.

reach.learn: Whether availability data shows which items to buy more of.

evidence.claim: A rental tool tracks availability and rental history per item, with barcode check-in.
Customer details in rental records are personal data; keep only what the rental needs.

assumptions: Boundary: from greeting to the rental choice; the contract is outside.
Input contract: items and barcodes registered by the branch manager; returns scanned by the clerks; fallback is the paper board.
Greeting and advice keep their full time. s3 keeps 30 for items not scanned or out of place. The clerk's return scan (s2r, share 1) keeps the screen current.
The shop rents equipment with many items of each type.
research_questions: Do customers wait less once availability is on screen?

incremental.description: No further upkeep: scanning returns is shown as step s2r, and items and barcodes are kept by the branch manager.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small shop where the clerk sees most stock from the counter (5.7); high: many items of each type out on rent (13.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Answer calls about prices and availability, take phone reservations, check availability, call back with answers and confirm by e-mail.

steps.what: Clerk answers telephones to provide information on prices, hours and availability
Customers reserve online on the shop's website
Clerk takes phone orders: written on paper today, typed into the rental system after the change, with fewer orders by phone
Clerk checks the reservation before confirming: item, dates, customer and contact details
Clerk checks availability while the caller waits
Clerk calls customers back with answers to technical questions
Clerk confirms the checked reservation to the customer: by a typed e-mail today, by one confirm in the rental system after the change

tasks.design: The shop's website shows prices, opening hours and live availability from the rental system ({OTHER}) and takes online reservations, so many calls fall away. Phone orders are typed straight into the rental system; the clerk checks each one and confirms it from there; technical questions still get a call back, and no voice bot answers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Prices and availability were only known at the counter, so customers phoned.
tasks.enabler_now: Rental systems track availability per item and take reservations.
tasks.still_hard: Trade customers often prefer to phone; prices with deposits need explaining.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what the caller really needs and suggesting the right machine.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; routine calls fall away.

reach.learn: Whether trade customers move to online booking.

evidence.claim: A rental tool tracks availability and rental history per item and takes reservations.
Shopping chatbots must tell customers they are AI; this design uses none.

assumptions: Boundary: from the call to the confirmation; collection of the item is outside.
Input contract: prices and opening hours kept by the branch manager in the rental system; availability from scanned returns; fallback is the phone.
Customer time, including online reservations (s1o, share 1), is outside the clerk's savings.

Technical call-backs and the reservation check keep their full time. s1 keeps 60 because many callers still want a person. s2 keeps 60 because about half the orders move online and the rest are still typed by the clerk. s3 keeps 30 because availability is on the screen. s5 keeps 10 for the confirm itself.
unknowns: Share of reservations that would move online.
research_questions: How many calls per day disappear when availability is online?

incremental.description: Clerk checks online reservations each morning.
Branch manager keeps online prices current.

approvals.approved_version: The reservation with item, dates and customer exactly as checked by the clerk in s2c, confirmed once by e-mail from the rental system to the customer's address on file; any change needs a new check and confirmation.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: trade customers keep phoning, so few calls and orders move online (30.0); high: about half the orders and most routine questions move online (46.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Fill in the rental contract, check ID and required licences, copy documents, explain the terms, get the customer's signature and file the contract.

steps.what: Clerk prepares rental forms by hand with customer, item, dates and deposit
Clerk checks ID and required licenses for the item
Clerk records the licence type and expiry date: by photocopying ID and licence today, by typing the two fields after the change
Clerk explains deposit, damage and return terms
Customer gives a signature on the contract
Clerk files the signed contract and enters it in the system

tasks.design: The rental contract is filled from the reservation and the customer's record in the rental system ({OTHER}); the clerk checks it. The clerk checks ID and licences by eye and records only the licence type and expiry date, no copies, and the customer signs on a tablet so the contract is stored at once; explaining the terms stays at the counter.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contracts were handwritten, documents photocopied and paper filed.
tasks.enabler_now: Rental systems keep reservations and customer records per item; tablet signatures are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Licence checks need a person; copying ID is only allowed where a law requires it.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting that a customer is not fit to take a trailer on the road.
tasks.altitude: The clerk checks a filled contract instead of writing one.

reach.learn: Whether signed digital contracts settle disputes faster.

evidence.claim: A rental tool keeps reservations and rental history per item with barcode check-in.
Copying ID documents is allowed only where a law requires it; otherwise record only what is needed.

assumptions: Boundary: from the rental choice to the filed contract; payment and deposit are outside.
Input contract: contract template and terms set by the branch manager; licence rules per item set by the branch manager; fallback is the paper form.
Customer time is outside the clerk's savings.

Licence checks and explaining terms keep their full time. s1 keeps 30 for checking the filled contract and typing walk-in customers. s3 keeps 30 for typing the licence type and expiry; no copies are kept. Filing goes because the signed contract is stored at once.
unknowns: Share of repeat customers with records.
research_questions: Do disputes about terms fall with signed digital contracts?

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep: the branch manager keeps the template and licence rules, and learning the tablet flow is a one-off.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many walk-in customers without a reservation or record, so most contracts are still typed (36.1); high: most rentals come from a reservation (51.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The rental clerk keeps advice, demonstration and checks; paper planning, contracts and routine calls shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A clerk who spends counter time advising customers, not writing forms or answering availability calls.
